kept.excerpt: McKinney had about $264,000 cash on hand to Thanedar's nearly $4.7 million, according to their July campaign finance reports. Waters and Democrat John Goci were disqualified for submitting insufficient voter signatures. Thanedar won 28% in the crowded 2022 congressional primary and 55% in the 2024 primary.
kept.publisher: Detroit Free Press, Clara Hendrickson (republished by AOL)
kept.relevance: This detailed local preview supplies the financial disparity, ballot consolidation and historical electoral baseline.

kept.excerpt: U.S. Rep. Summer Lee endorsed state Rep. Donavan McKinney on Monday in his bid to unseat U.S. Rep. Shri Thanedar. Lee is the first member of the Congressional Black Caucus to endorse a candidate in the race and the second sitting member of Congress to back McKinney, joining Rashida Tlaib. This year's primary is a one-on-one contest after two other Democratic candidates were disqualified.
kept.relevance: The report documents a recent expansion of McKinney's congressional support and the reduced risk of opposition vote splitting.

kept.excerpt: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark, and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar endorsed Shri Thanedar for re-election in Michigan's 13th Congressional District. Their joint statement praised his constituent service, efforts to lower family costs and opposition to President Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans.
kept.relevance: The dated report verifies national Democratic leadership support for the incumbent shortly before the primary.

kept.excerpt: Thanedar gave his campaign $800,000 in June and outraised McKinney last quarter, although his campaign carries his personal loans as debt. Two-thirds of the money Thanedar raised in the quarter came through AIPAC bundlers, according to his latest FEC filing. The campaign reported more than $630,000 in investment-income losses during the quarter.
kept.relevance: The investigation identifies the incumbent's self-financing capacity and fundraising composition while distinguishing those resources from investment losses.

kept.excerpt: A Justice Democrats email reported a new Data for Progress poll showing Thanedar leading McKinney 46% to 42%. The email also described a separate result after respondents were shown candidate biographies, with McKinney at 48% and Thanedar at 41%. Justice Democrats stated that it was supporting McKinney.
kept.publisher: Justice Democrats (dated email preserved by Archive of Political Emails)
kept.relevance: This contemporaneous partisan source preserves a pre-cutoff polling result, with the biography-conditioned response kept separate from the initial ballot test.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-22, inclusive. Selected seven items with verifiable publication dates no later than the cutoff; the official manual identifies its edition as July 2025, so month precision is retained. Article bodies and dates were checked with agent-reach after web_fetch failed. The Justice Democrats email's July 22, 2026, 6:41 PM date is visible in the archive's indexed metadata; its poll claims are attributed to a McKinney supporter, and the original questionnaire and full methodology were not independently verified. Excerpts are factual paraphrases of source content. Later-dated material, undated current-status pages, prediction markets, betting odds and market prices were excluded. No subsequent developments or primary outcome are included.
